in_arabic.name: ألفات

The pleasant meaning associated with sweet basil infuses the child with a beautiful and attractive disposition - a personality that is appealing and pleasing to those around them. The name also suggests a deep connection to nature, as basil is a common herb used in Middle Eastern cuisine and herbal medicine.

It is believed that sweetness of character and a pleasing fragrance of good deeds are essential to a true believer's spiritual growth. The name serves as a reminder to strive towards being a 'sweet basil' in one's local community - spreading fragrance, joy, and creating an atmosphere of kindness and love. historical_references.reference: Olfat bint Safee'ah was a renowned companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and a wife of Ali ibn Abi Talib. She is known for her extraordinary generosity and piety. During the Battle of Khaybar, when Ali (as) was leading the Muslim army to conquer the Jewish stronghold, Olfat offered herself as a human shield to protect her husband and his soldiers. Her self-sacrificing act saved many Muslim lives and became an inspiration for the Muslim community.
historical_references.context: Islamic History, Prophet Muhammad's Companions, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Battle of Khaybar

historical_references.reference: Olfat bint Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Bajiri was a 13th century Andalusian scholar and poetess, also known as 'Umm-ul-Banin' (Mother of Sons). She was a prominent figure in the Islamic Golden Age and is renowned for her contributions to Arabic literature. She wrote on various subjects, including Sufism, poetry, and mysticism. Her poetry is characterized by its deep spirituality and subtlety.
